cards.title: The Desk
cards.description: Your new desk at the Builders' Guild. A dormant golem sits in the corner with dark eyes. Scattered documents cover the surface — some current, some outdated. A badge reader blinks by the inner door. Pip waves from the hallway.

cards.title: Pip (Apprentice)
cards.description: A young apprentice with boundless energy. Pip explains spec-driven development and warns you about Marcus's vibe-coding habits.

cards.title: Architect's Badge
cards.description: A heavy brass badge engraved with the Builders' Guild crest. Opens the inner door to the Drafting Hall.

cards.title: Dormant Golem
cards.description: The golem's eyes are dark. It tries to speak: 'I... have no context. No specs. No connections to external guilds. The conduits were severed when Marcus left. I need three things: specs in my memory, and conduits reconnected to the Testing Guild and Diagram Guild.' Its voice fades to static.

cards.title: Sorted Papers
cards.description: The papers reveal Marcus never wrote specs — he told the golem 'build a social app' and got a different interpretation every time. Vibe coding works for prototypes but fails for production.

cards.title: Marcus's Farewell Note
cards.description: Scrawled on the back of a napkin: 'I'm done. The golem kept building the wrong thing because I never wrote proper specs. Then the client wanted testing and I had no conduits to the Testing Guild. The MCP pipes are disconnected — you'll need to rewire them in the Workshop. Good luck. — M'

cards.title: The Drafting Hall
cards.description: A long room with drafting tables. The left wall has a terminal. The right wall has a client communication screen. In the center: a large scroll frame waiting for structured specs.

cards.title: Lord Ashford
cards.description: A demanding client displayed on the communication screen. He wants a social platform — users post short messages, follow each other, and it works on mobile. Marcus gave him a cat adoption site instead.

cards.title: Project Specs
cards.description: Three structured requirements converted from Ashford's vague demands: user posting, following/feed, and responsive mobile performance. The golem can now build with precision.

cards.title: Marcus's Notes
cards.description: Spec-driven development produces three documents: Requirements (WHAT), Design (HOW), and Tasks (IN WHAT ORDER). Together they give the golem everything it needs.

cards.title: The Golem Workshop
cards.description: A circular chamber. The golem sits in the center, connected to conduit pipes on all sides. A monitor shows its build output — currently static. Document shelves line the walls. A pipe junction box connects to external guilds.

cards.title: Context Loaded
cards.description: The golem's memory is loaded with the correct documents — requirements.md, design.md, and tasks.md — fitting within its 2000-token context window. Poisoned docs excluded.

cards.title: MCP Connected
cards.description: Three conduits wired correctly: Testing Guild to Playwright Server, Diagram Guild to AWS Diagram Server, Documentation Guild to AWS Docs Server. The golem can now reach external tools.

cards.title: The Build Yard
cards.description: An open construction yard. The golem stands ready, glowing blue. A blueprint frame shows the architecture layers. A terminal awaits commands. The building foundation is laid but empty.

cards.title: First Command
cards.description: You issued the build command: 'build from design-specs'. The golem acknowledges and begins constructing from the structured specifications.

cards.title: Architecture Done
cards.description: Eight components placed on correct layers: React+Next.js and CloudFront on Presentation, Lambda and API Routes on Application, DynamoDB on Data, CDK Stack and IAM Roles on Infrastructure.

cards.title: Codebase Mapped
cards.description: You can't deploy frontend and backend simultaneously. The frontend needs the API URL which only exists AFTER the backend deploys. Phase 1: infrastructure. Phase 2: frontend with real URLs.

cards.title: The Launch Tower
cards.description: The top floor. A panoramic window shows the city below. A deployment console with a countdown timer. A test results screen. The golem stands at the controls, ready for final commands.

cards.title: Tests Ready
cards.description: Playwright test pipeline built in correct order: Navigate to URL → Click Login → Fill Form → Assert Feed Visible → Take Screenshot. The test suite is green.

cards.title: Deploy Sequence
cards.description: Two-phase deployment ordered correctly: CDK deploy infrastructure, extract API URL, rebuild frontend, deploy to S3, invalidate CloudFront cache. Ready to execute.

cards.title: Bug Found
cards.description: CORS error identified in the deployment logs — Access-Control-Allow-Origin header missing and POST /api/posts returning 403 from browser. The fix is clear.

cards.title: Deployment Runbook
cards.description: A laminated card pinned to the console: 'TWO-PHASE DEPLOY: 1) CDK deploy infrastructure (Lambda, DynamoDB, API Gateway). 2) Extract the API Gateway URL from CDK output. 3) Rebuild frontend with the real API URL baked in. 4) Deploy static assets to S3. 5) Invalidate CloudFront cache so users get the new version.'

cards.title: Launched!
cards.description: CORS headers added, API Gateway redeployed, tests passing. The CloudFront URL goes live. Lord Ashford sees a working social platform. The golem's eyes glow steady blue — it knows what it is now.
